talks.title: DC Groups January 2018 Community Update
talks.teaser: Jayson Street provides the January 2018 community briefing for DEF CON Groups, sharing organizer resources, event planning, and local chapter expansion.
talks.summary:
### The Evolution and Mission of DEF CON Groups
At 00:00, Jayson E. Street, Global Ambassador for DEF CON Groups (DCGs), welcomes the global hacker community to the January 2018 New Year status update. Broadcasting from an underground DEF CON museum and archive surrounded by historical conference badges, vintage posters, and hacker memorabilia, Street celebrates the rapid worldwide expansion of DEF CON Groups throughout 2017—highlighting new community chapters emerging everywhere from Dubai to Durban. He reiterates that DCGs exist as grassroots, community-run organizations designed to bring the spirit, education, and camaraderie of DEF CON into local municipalities year-round.

### Leadership and Global Coordination Updates
At 02:15 and 04:31, Street announces significant leadership developments, introducing Nikki White as the Lead DEF CON Groups Global Coordinator. He outlines how the centralized coordination team works to streamline group recognition, manage official portal listings, and supply organizational toolkits to regional leaders. This support structure helps newly founded groups establish sustainable local rhythms, organize regular physical meetups, and connect with other regional technology collectives.

### Upholding Codes of Conduct and Inclusivity
At 06:10, Street underscores the mandatory community standards governing official DCGs. He firmly stresses that all local chapters must enforce the conference Code of Conduct, cultivating welcoming, safe, and collaborative environments for hackers of all skill levels, professional backgrounds, and personal identities. Street warns against gatekeeping, elitism, and illegal activities, reminding organizers that DEF CON Groups are educational, non-commercial sanctuaries dedicated to collaborative research and defensive skill-building.

### Preserving Non-Commercial Hacker Spaces
At 07:15, the presentation emphasizes the strict policy against commercialization and sales pitches. Street reminds chapter leaders that DEF CON Group meetings must remain completely free to attend and devoid of corporate sponsorship interference or vendor vendor-lock-in product demonstrations. Groups should prioritize open hardware hacking, Capture the Flag (CTF) training, hands-on lab experimentation, and peer-to-peer lightning talks that empower attendees.

### Looking Ahead: Monthly Updates and DEF CON 26
Concluding between 07:45 and 09:01, Street pledges a new cadence of monthly video broadcasts to keep international group organizers informed and aligned. He encourages members to begin brainstorming and drafting Call for Papers (CFP) submissions for DEF CON 26 in Las Vegas, urging local chapters to showcase their regional security research on the international stage.
